findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: generate_contract, download_contract · Private data: list_contract_types, initiate_negotiation, download_contract, delete_deal, buy_credits, get_credit_balance, find_template, get_deadlines · Public sink: list_contract_types, share_with_attorney · Destructive: delete_deal.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: generate_contract, download_contract · Private data: list_contract_types, initiate_negotiation, download_contract, delete_deal, buy_credits, get_credit_balance, find_template, get_deadlines · Public sink: list_contract_types, share_with_attorney · Destructive: delete_deal

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_contract_types" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Every contract type Dealroom can make, with the code to use as contractType, the guide slug, the governing laws and languages it is offered in, the role the caller can take (DPA and BAA only) and the inputs it asks for. No API key needed." → after: "Every contract type Dealroom can make, with the code to use as contractType, the guide slug, the governing laws and languages it is offered in, the role the caller can take (DPA and BAA only) and the inputs it asks for. findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
